title: FoxGlove Health — triage assistant integration scratchbook
content:
Quick scribbles from discovery + ops call w/ FoxGlove Health (2026-02-27). Mostly raw capture; follow-up items at bottom.

High-level: mid-size telehealth vendor (~1200 clinicians), wants an LLM-powered triage assistant that helps intake patient symptoms, surface next-steps, and draft clinician notes. PHI involved — they need BAA, audit logs, end-to-end encryption, and HSM-backed KMS. Prefer private deployment in Azure (customer subscription, VNet peering).

Customer constraints / requirements captured:
- Throughput target: steady 30 req/s during business hours, spikes to 150 req/s during morning windows. Typical request size: 200-600 tokens. Target 95th pct latency < 300ms for token stream start (they want snappy UX).
- SLA/Compliance: HIPAA + SOC2. Must preserve audit trail for every request: user id, model version, input hash, response hash. Retention policy: 7 years for audit logs (legal ask) — storage implications.
- Data residency: Azure East US (primary); DR in West US. No cross-region processing without explicit consent.
- Auth/keys: customer wants HSM-managed keys (Azure Key Vault with HSM), need to demonstrate KMS integration and key rotation flow.
- Models: initial ask for high-quality summarization + instruction-following. They asked about Llama-2-70B quantized path, but worried about latency & cost. Proposed multi-tier routing: primary model = 13B/30B quantized for latency; fallback to larger 70B for complex cases or async batch. Need to validate quality gap on their transcript set.
- RAG: plan to use RAG against internal knowledge (policies, triage protocols). They currently use an internal Postgres + embedding store (we discussed Milvus vs PGVector). They prefer staying on Azure-managed DBs.
- Session persistence: multi-turn conversation with KV cache per session for up to 24h; customer wants session affinity to clinician apps (sticky routing).
- Security gotchas called out by their infra team:
  * No public IP inbound rules for model instances; prefer private link / VNet integration.
  * Egress to external vector DBs blocked by default (we need to show deployment with data plane inside customer VNet).
  * PCI not relevant but infra asked about sidecar logging — must ensure logs redact PHI before leaving network.

Performance / architecture notes (from suggested options):
- Batching: conservative batch sizes for interactive latency; autoscaling policy that prioritizes latency (scale up GPUs before increasing batch window).
- Prefix / KV cache: enable prefix cache for frequent templates (intake forms) to reduce compute. Validate memory footprint for 24h retention across 10k concurrent sessions.
- Quantization: recommend int8/4 baselining on internal benchmark for their seq lengths (avg 400). Expect CPU fallback to blow latency — must avoid.
- Fallback policy: model-variant fallback + async job submission if primary queue saturated (visible to user as "processing" state).

Open questions / risks:
- Will customer allow storing de-identified transcripts for model quality monitoring? Legal TBD.
- Exact retention window for request payloads vs logs (they asked for 7yr audit logs but are unclear on raw payload retention).
- How many unique templates and prompt families? impacts prefix cache hit rates. Need sample set.
- Network egress constraints might block telemetry/observability — need offline shipping or proxy plan.
- Milvus vs PGVector: which fits their operational preference? (they prefer Azure Postgres right now)

Action/next steps (assignments):
- [Mariana] Share minimal architecture sketch showing: VNet-peered deployment, KMS/HSM flow, private endpoints, and logging redaction approach. Due: 2026-03-03.
- [Theo] Run quick-model-quality pilot: 13B quantized vs 70B fp16 on a redacted sample of 200 transcripts. Produce top-level diff and latency numbers. Due: 2026-03-10.
- [Priya] Draft preliminary BAA checklist & retention guidance for legal; confirm if 7yr audit retention is realistic. Due: 2026-03-06.
- [FoxGlove] Send: redacted sample transcripts (200), list of triage templates, expected peak schedule. Ask: can they provide a spike-day log?
- Schedule: technical deep-dive with FoxGlove infra (30–45m) — propose 2026-03-08 or 2026-03-09.

Notes-to-self / quick pitfall reminders:
- Avoid promising full 70B interactive SLAs without capacity/benchmark evidence.
- Watch out for long-context costs (if they want 8k+ windows must estimate token costs).
- Need clear UX fallback language for clinicians if async processing is used (so they don’t retry).

Attachments to prepare before deep-dive:
- Short benchmark doc: latency vs throughput for 13B/30B/70B (quantized vs fp16) on A100 vs H100 profiles.
- Sample deployment diagram showing private-link + KMS + observability pipeline with redaction step.
- Short checklist for infra (open ports, subnet sizing, storage for audit logs).

End of scratchbook. Will convert select pieces into a polished proposal once pilot numbers from Theo arrive.
